names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 23 Ιουνίου, which prints the company as «Άγιοι Ευστόχιος ο Πρεσβύτερος, Γάϊος ο ανεψιός του, και τα παιδιά αυτού Λολλία, Πρόβη και Ουρβανός»; the form above is this member's bare name, with the rank word and the relationship left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 23. јун ст. ст., „Свети мученици Евстохије, Гај и други с њима“ — Свети is not a rank and мученици is the rank, which `types` already carries; the first of the two bare forenames is what is left, and the heading gives him no see, no place and no by-name. The display name is the bare «Eustochius» and §6 keeps the rank out of the stored form. `foldchk.py` returns NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM and `.tmp/sr-foldpred.mjs` returns no other holder of the gate’s own folded key, **which is the surprise of the day**: the corpus keeps a second Eustochius, `eustochius-15-november`, and its Serbian row is still `undocumented` with no `sr` form on the folder at all, so the fold that looks certain is not one and no `READ_FOLDS` key is owed. Measured on both instruments, not suspected.

Read out of the name link behind this place in days.pravoslavie.ru's line for 23 июня ст. ст., «Евстохий Садонский, Анкирский, сщмч.», with the grade word left off; both epithets are the calendar's own. The calendar writes the form in the masculine, which is the reading recorded in this folder's russian row.

death.note: saint.gr's heading for each of the five in this company: «(; - 300)», and its narrative «υπήρξαν στα χρόνια των βασιλέων Μαξιμιανού και Αγρίππα κατά το έτος 300 μ.Χ.».

feast.note: The same menologion number this folder's other venerated rows carry. The one life page days.pravoslavie.ru gives the company, life1381, heads «День памяти: 23 июня» and names no other day; it was read whole and its account agrees with what this folder already carries — the pagan priest converted and baptised by the bishop of Antioch, the nephew and his whole household won at Lystra, the governor at Ancyra, and the beheading under Maximian — so no paragraph was added. ONE DISAGREEMENT BETWEEN SOURCES IS RECORDED AND NOT RESOLVED: the Russian calendar gives all five names in the masculine and calls the three of the household «отроков», lads, where the sources behind this corpus's display names make two of them daughters of the nephew. The identification rests on the company, the kinship, Lystra, Ancyra, the day and the number of names, and not on the gender of the forms; the display names were left as they stood. The day line closes «и иных», and with others, who are not named, so no further folder follows from it.

The page's own narrative gives second forms for four of the five names — Γάϊος ή Γαϊανός, Λολλία ή Λουλώ, Ουρβανός ή Ουρβάσιος — and those variants are not stored, only the form the day's line prints. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 06.07.2026 (23. јун ст. ст.) — „Свети мученици Евстохије, Гај и други с њима“

attestations.note: The day’s second entry, the first of the two men its heading names. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of this wave is. The Julian 23 June is the same menologion number this folder’s other venerated rows carry, so there is no second day and no §4 note is owed. **§5 ON THE HEADING, AND WHY FIVE FOLDERS TAKE A ROW OFF A HEADING THAT ENUMERATES TWO.** The heading „Свети мученици Евстохије, Гај и други с њима“ enumerates two bare forenames and then says и други с њима, and others with them. The body names the others: „Његов сродник Гај крсти се заједно са три отрока: Провом, Лолијем и Урбаном.“ And then „Сви ови, и још други уз њих, беху изведени пред суд, мучени и посечени због вере у Христа Господа у Листри.“ — all these, and still others besides them, were brought before the court, tortured and beheaded for the faith in Christ the Lord at Lystra. So five men of this entry have folders and all five take a row, which is the shape the Julian 25 May was read in: three names enumerated, и други after them, and two more named only in the body. The heading is quoted **whole** on all five, as §4 requires. Nobody is counted who is not named, and the others besides them get no folder and no row, there being nothing to make one out of — a narrated martyrdom with no name takes neither. **`dates` UNTOUCHED ON ALL FIVE.** This book gives no year of any kind. „Би Евстохије жрец идолски у време цара Максимијана, па видећи јунаштво хришћанских мученика, одбаци незнабоштво и крсти се.“ dates the beginning only у време цара Максимијана, in the time of the emperor Maximian, and **an emperor is no source for a year and a reign is not a date**. The five folders keep saint.gr’s `death` 300, which this book neither confirms nor contradicts, and no field moves on any of them. The emperor takes no row. **THE PLACE OF THE DEATH DISAGREES, AND BOTH ARE WRITTEN.** saint.gr, in these folders’ own prose, has Eustochius tortured at Lystra and then taken with Gaius and the children to Agrippinus — or, as others have it, Agrippa — the governor of Ancyra, and all of them beheaded there. This book has them beheaded at **Lystra** itself, „Сви ови, и још други уз њих, беху изведени пред суд, мучени и посечени због вере у Христа Господа у Листри.“ and names no governor, no Ancyra and no city of the Ousades. Neither account is chosen. No `locations`: Lystra and Antioch are named in clauses. **NO NEW `related` ROWS.** All five folders already carry the other four, in both directions, and this book confirms every one of them; nothing is added and nothing is touched. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse. THE VERSE IS NOT USED. The ПЕСМА for 23 June is twenty-two lines on the first entry alone and nothing at all on the second, third or fourth: it calls Agrippina purer than the lily, has her chant psalms in her wounds and bless her persecutors, has the angel come down when her bones are broken, and ends by asking her prayers. It is Bishop Nikolai’s own verse and not the entry’s account, so §3 of this wave’s brief puts it in no field and in no life, and it is recorded here instead. **That it versifies one of four entries is worth the line**: the verse is no index of what a day holds. **WHAT THIS DAY REFUSES, AND IT REFUSES A WHOLE ENTRY TWICE OVER.** The Prologue prints four entries for the Julian 23 June and only two of them are people. The third, „Спомен иконе Пресвете Богородице Владимирске“, is the commemoration of the Vladimir icon of the Mother of God and a feast and not a folder, by the standing ruling; its body is about a battle, not a life, and the two men in it — the Tatar khan Ahmet and the prince Ivan Vasilyevich who went out with the army — are neither of them saints of the entry and neither takes a row. The fourth, „Повест о покајању Теофила“, is **the shape this wave has not met before**: a heading that is not a commemoration at all but a tale, «a story of the repentance of Theophilus», about a man who out of envy signed away his soul, repented, wept forgiveness out of the Most Pure after a forty-day fast, got his paper back and confessed in church, and whose face shone like the sun when the bishop absolved him; it ends by saying God does not only forgive true penitents but numbers them among the saints. **No folder, on two grounds at once.** It is not a saint’s heading: there is no rank word in it, the noun it leads with is a tale and the person is in the genitive after it. And **Ruling 3**: `ls saints | grep -i theophil` returns twenty-three Theophilus folders and not one of them is this man — no penitent, nobody on 23 June, nobody of Adana, and `grep -l enitent saints/*/saint.json` returns five folders of which none is a Theophilus. He is named here and left out of the prose, and no row and no folder is made for him. **`types` UNTOUCHED, AND THIS BOOK TAKES THE PRESBYTER AWAY RATHER THAN GIVING IT.** The heading gives Свети, not a rank, and мученици, which is the `martyr` he carries. „Евстохије жрец идолски“ makes him a priest of the idols — a rank in the wrong religion and no word in this corpus’ vocabulary. And where saint.gr has him baptised and then **ordained presbyter**, which is where the folder’s `presbyter` and its slug come from, this book stops at the baptism: „Крсти га сам епископ антиохијски Евдоксије.“ — the bishop of Antioch Eudoxius baptised him himself — and no ordination appears anywhere in the entry. **The `presbyter` is not removed**: it is the Greek page’s reading and a silence is not a denial. Nothing is added either. Recorded, not resolved. **THE BAPTIZER TAKES NO ROW.** `ls saints | grep -i eudox` returns `eudoxius-of-melitene`, `eudoxius-of-sebasteia`, `eudoxia-daughter-of-athanasia`, `macarius-companion-of-eudoxius`, `soldiers-martyred-with-eudoxius` and `zeno-companion-of-eudoxius`, and not one of them is a bishop of Antioch; an identification off a name in another man’s life is not an identification. **Ruling 3**: named here, no folder, no row. The name is already in this folder’s prose off saint.gr, and `grep -ho '"display_name": "[^"]*"' saints/*/saint.json` returns no folder whose display name is the bare string «Eudoxius» — **measured before the prose was drafted, because §6’s trap is exactly that**, and the same grep is why nothing on this day names a famous man without checking him first. It also returned two bare display names that do belong to this entry: «Eustochius» is this folder’s own, and «Gaius» is **`gaius-pope-of-rome`’s** — so the bare word Gaius in a life matches a pope and not the man of this company, and every life written today names him by the linked display name on first mention. „После тога Евстохије постепено преведе своју родбину у хришћанство.“ — after his baptism he brought his kinsfolk over to Christianity by degrees, which is this book’s own bridge to the rest of the company and a sentence saint.gr does not have.
